subject: Follow-up: model mix & pricing (token volumes + unit economics)
messages:

Subject: Follow-up: model mix & pricing (token volumes + unit economics)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can size costs and next steps: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary product flows: customer chat (conversational UI), background embeddings for search & personalization, and occasional reranking for results pages.
- Key unknowns we need to finalize pricing: expected monthly token volumes by model type, target budget range, and whether you care about absolute target $/1M tokens for planning reserved capacity.

What we (Redwood) need from you to produce a firm quote
1) Monthly token volumes (approx) broken out by: chat (generation + context), embeddings (indexing vs online queries), and rerank (short scoring calls). If you only have ranges that's fine.
2) Target budget range or target $/1M tokens (helps us pick model variants and whether to recommend Dedicated).
3) Any latency/SLA constraints (esp for chat) or data residency constraints we should factor in.

Ballpark unit-econ examples (to help you bias answers):
- Chat (conversational generation): target $/1M tokens we commonly model between $10–$25 depending on model family and optimizations; for early sizing assume $15/1M.
- Embeddings (indexing + queries): target $/1M tokens assumption $5/1M for planning.
- Rerank (short scoring calls): target $/1M tokens assumption $10/1M.

Example ask: if you told us chat = 20M tokens/mo, embeddings = 5M, rerank = 2M, rough monthly cost at the assumptions above would be: (20*$15) + (5*$5) + (2*$10) = $300 + $25 + $20 = ~$345/mo. This is just a starting point — we can lower unit cost materially with batching/kv-caching/Dedicated commitments.

Next steps
- Can you reply with best-estimate monthly volumes + a target monthly budget range (or target $/1M)?
- If you want, we can run a simple spreadsheet (attached) with 3 scenarios (PoC, scale, enterprise) and show Dedicated vs hosted unit costs.

Attaching a quick pricing worksheet (ACME-pricing-v1.xlsx) — I populated the example numbers above so you can edit.

Thanks — cc'ing Dev (SE) and Rishi (sales eng) for any technical or contract follow-up.

Cheers,

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few quick numbers from our side after syncing with product/infra: 
- Chat (conversational): ~20M tokens/month (60% of the query volume) — mostly short back-and-forth sessions with an average response size ~120 tokens.
- Embeddings: ~6M tokens/month (indexing spikes + ~2.5M queries/mo online) — indexing is a one-time batch but will be repeated monthly for some datasets.
- Rerank: ~3M tokens/month (used on high-value search flows).

Budget range: we have an initial budget band of $1k–$5k/mo for this pilot. If unit economics are compelling we can scale quickly.

Question: how sensitive are your unit costs to model family? For chat we might accept a slightly lower-quality open model if the unit <> cost tradeoff is strong.

Appreciate the workbook — I looked quickly and will dig in.

—Jordan

Jordan — thanks for the numbers, that makes the sizing straightforward. I updated the attached worksheet (ACME-pricing-v1.xlsx) with three scenarios and a cost breakdown using conservative unit-econ assumptions we discussed on the call. Key notes below: 

Unit economics used for the worksheet (editable):
- Chat: $15 per 1M tokens
- Embeddings: $5 per 1M tokens
- Rerank: $10 per 1M tokens

Cost estimate using your volumes (chat 20M / embeddings 6M / rerank 3M):
- Chat: 20 * $15 = $300
- Embeddings: 6 * $5 = $30
- Rerank: 3 * $10 = $30
- Total: ~$360/month (hosted, baseline assumptions)

Observations / recommendations:
- Your stated pilot budget ($1k–$5k/mo) easily covers the hosted baseline; we expect production costs to rise as you index more content, but there are clear levers to control unit cost (model mix, quantization, Dedicated commits).
- If you target lower per-1M token pricing, two levers we typically use: (1) switch to a lower-cost model variant for less critical chat paths; (2) Dedicated/reserved capacity (we can offer discounted unit rates at commit tiers >200M tokens/mo).

Next steps
1) Confirm the volumes above are the right baseline (or give ranges).
2) Let us know if you want a Dedicated pricing example (I can route to our capacity team).
3) Quick tech check: Dev, can you confirm the embeddings pipeline notes below and whether we should recommend pre-computing vectors to reduce active token spend?

Spreadsheet attached: ACME-pricing-v1.xlsx (contains scenario tabs and a per-model cost calculator).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min follow-up if helpful.

Best,

Jordan — quick technical notes (TL;DR: we can likely reduce the effective chat and embedding spend by ~20–40% with standard optimizations):

- Chat: batching + KV caching for repeated system prompts and user history reduces token generation work. For short sessions your average per-session token multiply goes down with batching by up to ~30% depending on concurrency. Also look at serving a smaller chat-optimized model for low-risk paths.
- Embeddings: separate indexing (offline) from online query embeddings. Pre-computing vectors for the full corpus and only computing real-time embeddings for new content/query re-writes reduces active token spend. For your volumes, this typically halves the online token footprint.
- Rerank: these are short, high-QPS calls — choose a model variant optimized for scoring (lower context length) and we can recommend a quantized 8-bit profile to lower cost without materially impacting scores.

If you can confirm whether you expect heavy realtime indexing (many new docs/day) or mostly static indexes, I can add concrete tokenizer/token estimates to the workbook. Also happy to join a call to walk the team through the optimizations.

—Dev Patel
